gates: Every input field resolves to an official NBA page or the official injury PDF.
A third-party or unreachable source may not silently fill a competitive input.
No required input is blank. A blank anywhere fails the strategy for that slate.
Blank ≠ zero. The prior build's rule, kept.
≥ 10 official games observed by BOTH teams before a line may be graded above C.
Below ~10 games the shrink weight λ drops under ~0.75 and the line is mostly league mean.
Two independent ratings (net points/game; NetRtg) must imply spreads within 2.0 pts.
Two estimators that disagree mean the model is unstable, not that there is an edge.
PF/PA total and per-100×pace total must be within 4.0 pts.
Large gaps flag pace/defence inconsistencies that would poison a totals bet.
A dated, sourced price for the exact line must exist before a pick is staked.
Without a price there is no edge, no stake size and no ROI. Currently FAILS for every line.
≥ 300 settled bets of the strategy's own signals, settled from official box scores.
300 bets is the point at which a 55% hit rate separates from 52.4% at 5% one-sided.
Signals fitted on the first 70% of the backtest window must hold on the last 30%.
Every team the strategy relies on must be inside the luck noise band (|z| ≤ 1.96).
A signal leaning on a lucky record is measuring luck.
No parlay priced by multiplying legs unless the leg correlation is measured or bounded.
Same-game legs are not independent; the error is one-sided and expensive.
Inputs must be dated within 24 h of the slate, and the injury report within its filing window.
Teams must file by 5 p.m. local the day before, and 11 a.m.–1 p.m. on game day.
No input timestamped after the decision time may enter that decision.
The single most common way a profitable backtest is fake.

strategies.name: Consensus-rating side
strategies.signal: Bet the side implied by the average of two shrunk ratings when both estimators agree ≤1.0 pt.
strategies.why: The line itself is derivable from official data; the bet cannot be, because there is no price and no backtest.

strategies.name: Total mean-reversion
strategies.signal: Compare our total against the market total; act only on a ≥3.0 pt gap.
strategies.why: Our total exists (two estimators, ≤4.25 pt gap observed). The half of the comparison that is a price does not.

strategies.name: Two-leg cross-game parlay
strategies.signal: Two independent games, each leg passing S1, both legs at the same price level.
strategies.why: Cross-game independence is a stated assumption, not a measurement; and the compounded hold makes it worse than two singles at equal edge.

strategies.name: Same-game spread+total
strategies.signal: Home cover and over in the same game, priced with a measured joint distribution.
strategies.why: The joint probability is not the product. With no per-game data the correlation cannot be estimated, and a ±26% price error was already demonstrated in the prior build.

strategies.name: Player prop (points/rebounds/assists)
strategies.signal: Player season rate × expected minutes, compared with a posted line.
strategies.status: BLOCKED — no minutes or game-log data
strategies.why: Season PPG exists officially; a per-game distribution and a minutes floor do not. Without them there is no probability, only an average.

strategies.name: Prop combo (points+rebounds)
strategies.signal: Same-player correlation measured, then joint probability computed.
strategies.status: BLOCKED — same-player correlation requires box scores
strategies.why: This is the product the brief asks for most directly, and it is the one most dependent on the missing data.

strategies.name: Injury-availability fade
strategies.signal: When a listed starter is Out, re-price with a measured replacement effect.
strategies.status: BLOCKED — no on/off or usage data
strategies.why: Status is official and dated; the size of the effect is not available. The prior build correctly left the impact blank.

leaderboard: Log-loss on settled bets, not win rate
Win rate rewards luck on small samples; log-loss is a proper scoring rule, so honest probabilities beat lucky ones.
Below that the 95% interval on a 55% hit rate includes 50%.
Every submitted strategy counts, including discarded ones
Otherwise a submitter re-rolls variants until one looks good; the family-wise error rate explodes.
A pick must be published before tip and be sealed with a hash
Prevents back-filling a winning pick after the result is known.
Stake in units of bankroll, capped at 1% per bet
Keeps the leaderboard a skill measure rather than a leverage measure.
100 units: 50 to the top log-loss score over a full season, 30 split across the next three, 20 held in escrow for out-of-sample validation
Pays for demonstrated calibration, not a hot streak.
Any pick without a pre-tip timestamp, any settlement not from an official box score, any strategy edited after settlement begins
Removes the three ways a leaderboard is usually gamed.

Keep two independent estimators and publish their disagreement as the primary confidence signal, rather than a single blended rating.
This build shows a 0.999 correlation between the two, and a max 1.0-pt disagreement — which is itself evidence the model is stable. If the two ever diverge, that divergence is the signal.
Pin home-court advantage to the measured home-win rate instead of fitting it freely.
Unconstrained, σ and h trade off almost perfectly (σ 9→13 with h +7.9→0 fits equally well). Pinning h uses a quantity actually measured over 173 games and leaves one free parameter.
Needs a larger home-game sample to shrink the ±0.076 interval.
Report luck as a z-score per team and refuse to publish a strategy that leans on a team outside the noise band.
This build: 0 of 30 teams are outside |z| ≤ 1.96. So no signal may currently claim a team is 'overperforming its underlying level' — the data does not support it.
Add a market-anchored prior: blend the model line with the closing line, weight by measured out-of-sample log-loss.
A pure model line is usually worse than the market. Blending is the standard way to improve on both — but it needs the price data in SG-3 and the backtest in SG-2.
Model the total as possessions × points-per-possession, not as an average of team scoring averages.
The two total estimators in this build disagree by up to 4.25 pts, mostly on pace outliers. A possession model forces the identity to hold and makes the gap diagnostic.
Never multiply legs. Publish a correlation bound and a worst-case price, or refuse the parlay.
At 0.50/0.50 legs a 0.40 correlation moves the joint from 25.0% to 32.0% (+28%). Two books can differ by more than the edge.
The bound is currently a sensitivity band, not a measurement — needs SG-2.
Store every injury PDF with its timestamp and diff consecutive reports to detect status changes.

This is the only way to turn an injury into a line move. Without it, injury analysis stays qualitative.

The v1 build was not reproducible from a clean checkout. Two published values were state dependent: build_is_idempotent recorded whether a previous site.json happened to exist (False on a clone, True on a rebuild of the same inputs), and generated_at_utc reused the previous stamp only when a previous file existed. A fresh clone therefore could never reproduce the committed artefact, and every local full-suite run silently rewrote data/site.json.

Fixed: build_is_idempotent now reports the property by construction, and the stamp is derived from the newest retrieved_at_utc recorded inside the committed snapshots, so it is a function of the committed bytes rather than of mtime or the clock.
